newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech shares begin to lose steam as PSE sputters.
newsitem.headline: Czech shares begin to lose steam as PSE sputters.

text.p: The Prague Stock Exchange lost ground on Wednesday for the first time in four sessions as a wave of bearish sentiment washed away the market's few remaining bulls.

Financial shares, at the heart of recent gains, retreated on a round of profit-taking, pushing the PX50 index down 3.3 points, or 0.61 percent, to 533.9, while the Reuters RPIX index eased six points to 1,089.
Overall, 161 issues gained, 153 lost and 88 were unchanged. Total volume was heavier at 940,964 shares on turnover of 681.1 million crowns.
Komercni Banka, Zivnostenska Banka, IPB and insurer Ceska Pojistovna all lost ground on the day.
For IPB, its 10 crown loss was the first session since the government announced the bank would be the first of the four major banks to be privatised.

Even though no details of a possible sell off were announced, investors seized on the statement as the signal they had been looking for that a foreign strategic partner would be the most likely beneficiary of any sell off, making the bank's shares attractive to other smaller investors.
Since the announcement, Nomura and ING Bank have been rumoured as the frontrunners in any bid to participate in the selloff. The government holds about a 30 percent stake in IPB.
But analysts said that the bubble caused by the anno uncement was over, and there were few fundamentals to push the market further.

"Corporate results just aren't that good so far, and there are few reasons for foreign investors to enter the market at this point. Instead, most are looking to Poland or Hungary," said one U.S.-based analyst.
"I don't expect to see the market move much higher over the next few months," he added.
